The picks

Chosen for the recipient and use described, using published product information. We have not hands-on tested these products.

  1. 1. Pilots who take paper notes

    SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

    Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

    Keep in mind
    Its utility is limited for someone who keeps all notes digitally.
    Before you choose
    Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.
    $24.50Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  2. 2. Students whose instructor recommends this format

    ASA pilot logbook

    An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

    Keep in mind
    Another logbook can be redundant if they have a preferred paper book or digital system.
    Before you choose
    Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.
    $9.49Listed 2026-10-20View at Pilot Mall↗
  3. 3. Students learning paper navigation

    ASA CP-1 Fixed Plotter

    A small, inexpensive tool with chart scales and a course protractor.

    Keep in mind
    Duplicates a tool many school starter kits already contain.
    Before you choose
    Match the chart scale and the instructor’s equipment list.
    $10.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗
  4. 4. Pilots wanting a compact red/white light

    Smith & Wesson Night Guard Dual-Beam Light

    Separate red and white light options make it more specific than a novelty flashlight.

    Keep in mind
    Light controls and battery preferences are personal; do not assume it replaces required equipment.
    Before you choose
    Confirm batteries, controls and the pilot’s equipment list before purchase.
    $18.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗

    P-40 Warhawk Crew Socks

    Shark-mouth graphics make an inexpensive everyday accessory aircraft-specific.

    Keep in mind
    Patterned socks are a style choice and sizing still matters.

    Flying Ace Snoopy Clip-On

    Keep in mind
    Larger than a conventional metal keyring and can catch on a crowded bag.

    $13.99Listed 2026-10-21View at Pilot Mall↗

Choose one good match

The goal is not to assemble as many aviation-themed things as possible. A pilot who writes paper notes may appreciate a multifunction pen more than a box of novelty items. Someone who loves airshows may get more enjoyment from a Blue Angels ornament. Start with how they spend their time, then use price to narrow the options. A short explanation of why you picked the item can make an inexpensive gift feel considered.

Useful gifts for a flight bag

The SKILCRAFT B3 combines two ink colors with a pencil, making it a straightforward option for a paper-note user. A compact red-and-white light is another possibility, especially if you know their current one needs replacing. Neither requires choosing a major aircraft component, but preferences still matter. Ask what they already own. A bag tag is inexpensive and easy to pair with a handwritten card for a working pilot.

Personal gifts for off-duty time

Clothing and ornaments can make good low-budget gifts when the reference is right. A Cessna 182 shirt is particularly relevant to someone who flies or admires the Skylane. Do not substitute it for a 172-specific gift without checking the connection. With apparel, leave room in the budget for shipping and select a seller with suitable exchange terms. A cap avoids some shirt-sizing uncertainty, though fit and style are still personal.

Budget does not remove compatibility checks

An inexpensive kneeboard can still be the wrong purchase if it does not fit the recipient’s tablet and case. A logbook can be redundant if a school already supplies one. Check with the pilot or instructor before buying either. It is better to spend a little less on the right item than to buy something technical simply because it appears to be a deal.

Keep the delivered price under your limit

The prices shown are product prices in US dollars, not guaranteed checkout totals. Shipping can be a large share of a small order. Compare the delivered total and avoid adding unrelated items just to reach a free-shipping threshold. If you are buying several small gifts from one retailer, a combined order may make sense, but the final choice should still fit each recipient.

Prices and availability can change. Check the exact model, delivered total and return terms with the seller. Our recommendations are researched editorial selections, not hands-on test results.
